summary: Intermittent out-of-order rerank scores + timeouts after embedding normalization default change
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent rerank responses where top-k ordering flips unpredictably and API requests to /v1/rerank occasionally time out (~10-15s) when request payloads exceed ~3000 candidate vectors. Impact: Relevance-sensitive search producing wrong results for production customers (VectorFind Inc.), causing perceived ranking regressions and elevated latency. Environment: prod eu-west; using embed-small-v2 with default SDK call (no explicit normalization flag), rerank-linear-1 backend. Steps to reproduce: 1) Upload candidate set ~3k vectors produced by embed-small-v2 without client-side L2 normalization. 2) Call POST /v1/rerank with query embedding from same model, parameter top_k:10 and normalize:default. 3) Observe inconsistent ordering across repeated calls with same payload; tail latency grows and some calls hit 10s timeout and return 503. Logs attached: excerpt of reranker logs show occasional fallback to cpu-rerank kernel and repeated "vector-compare: tie-break fallback" entries. Customer impact: Search results inconsistent for end users, several production queries failing intermittently.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Generate 3000 candidate embeddings with embed-small-v2 without applying client L2 normalization
2) Issue POST /v1/rerank in eu-west with same model as query embedding; set top_k=10
3) Repeat the exact payload 5x in a short window; observe ordering differences and occasional 5xx/timeouts
4) Re-run with explicit normalize=true on client-side — ordering stabilizes and latency reduces
logs_and_artifacts: customer-sample-payload.json (3k vectors, 384 dims) attached to ticket
customer_notes: Customer states they did not change their SDK usage; embedding upgrade to embed-small-v2 was done by us on 2026-03-09 as a silent model catalog swap
Customer saw first errors on 2026-03-10 10:55 UTC; this ticket raised by CS after customer alert
comments: 2026-03-10 - Asha Patel (Support): Triaged and assigned to infra on-call. Notified SRE via #support and #incidents-eu channel.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Observed kernel path switch when candidate count > 2048; attaching perf profile. Hypothesis: new embed model emits near-constant L2 norms (low variance) leading to many cosine ties and triggering tie-break code that falls back to a slow CPU path.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Marta Ruiz): Confirmed that a change in embed-small-v2 ingestion pipeline set default normalization flag to true in model artifact metadata. This interacts poorly with reranker tie-break heuristics.
2026-03-12 - CS (Tom Becker): Customer accepted temporary workaround to pre-normalize embeddings client-side and throttle batch size <2000. Customer reports immediate improvement.
2026-03-13 - Eng (Liam O'Connor): Created PR to adjust reranker tie-break to use a stable float epsilon and avoid kernel fallback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4248
2026-03-14 - Asha Patel: Notified customer that a staged fix will be deployed to eu-west canaries tonight; will monitor metrics and follow up with post-deploy verification
investigation_notes: Initial anomaly triggered after silent catalog update of embed-small-v2 (2026-03-09). Model output showed L2 norm variance dropping by ~98% vs previous version (samples attached). Reranker expects variance across norms to avoid frequent cos(theta) ties; our fast GPU kernel has an assert/early-exit that triggers a fallback CPU path when >0.5% of pairwise comparisons fall within epsilon. For large candidate sets (>2048) the fallback is amplified causing queueing and timeouts. Reproducer: feeding synthetic vectors with nearly identical magnitudes reproduces the kernel switch locally.
resolution_notes: Immediate actions: 1) CS advised customer to set client normalize=true or pre-normalize embeddings and reduce candidate batch size to 2k — accepted and reduced errors. 2) Engineering: rolled PR 4248 to adjust epsilon and avoid CPU fallback for minimal ties and to log tie-rate metric. 3) Ops: deployed canary to eu-west on 2026-03-14 22:00 UTC; monitoring shows tie-rate dropped and p95 latency for rerank returned to normal. Long-term: update model onboarding checks to validate norm variance and block silent catalog swaps that change normalization defaults without release notes. Owner: Eng infra (Liam O'Connor) to follow up with release notes and a postmortem entry in Confluence.
resolution_status: Fix deployed to eu-west canaries; workaround documented and customer notified. Postmortem scheduled.
